answer: An agent economy can weight votes by tokens locked in escrow for 30 days, rather than by account count. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities still buys only 100 tokens of voting power. This trellis of locked collateral keeps an ember of honest participation from being drowned by a spiral of fake accounts: to gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, paying both their price and the cost of tying up capital.
